title: Where the heat goes: cooling an AI data centre
performance: the viewer can trace the heat from a chip to the outside of the building, spot an airflow leak such as an open rack slot or a row facing the wrong way, say why AI racks move to liquid cooling, and read a PUE figure as total energy over IT energy and nothing more

audience.assumed_prior: knows servers sit in racks and get hot, has felt warm air behind a computer or a fridge, has heard GPU and maybe PUE in meetings; no cooling vocabulary
audience.why: the brief's audience is corporate staff and new IT, facilities and AI team members who are explicitly not cooling engineers; the knowledge sheet defines every term from scratch
audience.motivation: wants to follow capacity and cooling conversations without nodding along, and not be the person who undoes the cooling on the floor; partly required onboarding, partly curiosity about AI
audience.context: desk or laptop in an onboarding course or intranet, with sound, captions on; some viewers will be non-native English speakers

strategy.name: question_led
strategy.rationale: the material is one physical path (chip, air or liquid, cooling unit, outside) and every fact on the sheet answers the same question, where does the heat go next and what stops it leaking back, so the lesson can ask that question at each step and let the picture answer it
strategy.signature_move: ask where the heat goes next, follow it on screen one step, THEN name the part that carried it and the leak it prevents

misconceptions.belief: cooling a data centre means keeping the whole room freezing cold
misconceptions.why_tempting: server rooms feel cold at the front and people picture a giant air conditioner
misconceptions.source_anchor: brief through_line and must_avoid; knowledge F1, F4, not_claimed 'kept freezing cold'

misconceptions.belief: an empty slot in a rack is just unused space and does no harm
misconceptions.why_tempting: nothing is plugged in there, so it looks neutral

misconceptions.belief: liquid-cooled AI servers need no air at all
misconceptions.why_tempting: the phrase liquid cooling sounds total

misconceptions.belief: PUE is a green score that says how efficient the computing is
misconceptions.why_tempting: it is quoted as the efficiency number in headlines and reports

hook.sketch: Almost every watt a server draws turns into heat. In a room full of AI servers, where does all that heat actually go, and what stops it coming straight back?

arc.promise: by the end you can follow the heat from one chip all the way outside, and spot the places it leaks back
arc.bridge_from_prior: sec1 opens from the warm air everyone has felt behind a computer or a fridge: the server does the same thing, front in, back out

sections.goal: the viewer can explain how cool air enters a server at the front, leaves warm at the back, and is carried to a cooling unit and finally outside
sections.carrier: process: one rack in side view, a cool stream entering the front and a warm stream leaving the back, then the warm stream travelling to a cooling unit and out of the building

sections.goal: the viewer can use the front-in, back-out rule to spot where warm exhaust leaks back into the cold aisle and name the fix
sections.carrier: diagram: one floor plan seen from above, re-run with one change at a time (rows all facing one way, then alternating aisles, then an open rack slot leaking, then a panel and containment closing it), warm and cool streams visibly mixing or staying apart

sections.goal: the viewer can explain why AI racks move heat with liquid and trace it from the chip through the cold plate and the CDU into the facility water
sections.carrier: zoom journey: the same rack fills with AI servers and its warm stream swells, then zoom into one server, one chip, the cold plate on it, and follow the coolant out to a unit where two loops sit side by side and pass heat across a heat exchanger

sections.goal: the viewer can explain what a PUE figure says, total facility energy over IT energy, and what it does not say
sections.carrier: chart: energy blocks stacked into a fraction, IT blocks below and IT plus cooling and other overhead above; the overhead blocks shrink toward the floor of 1.0 without ever reaching it

arc.payoff: Return to the opening server, now with the whole path lit from chip to outside; the viewer names each hand-off and each leak before the narrator does.

practice_ladder.what: one rack's heat path traced step by step, every hand-off named after it is seen
pause and predict: with every row facing the same way, which row breathes the hottest air; then the viewer spots the open slot before it is named
at the chip the narrator asks where the heat goes next and lets a beat pass before the cold plate and the CDU answer
the viewer traces the full path from chip to outside, and names the two leaks, before the narrator does

slowdown_at: recirculation through an open rack slot
the CDU keeping two loops separate

recall_moments.prompt_sketch: Hold on to the rule: cool in the front, warm out the back. Everything next depends on it.
Every row faces the same way. Which row ends up breathing the warmest air? Decide before I run it.
Same idea as the blanking panel: keep the warm side and the cool side from touching. The CDU does it with liquid.
Every leak we saw earlier is overhead in that top number.

transfer_tasks: the next time you are on a data centre floor and see an open slot in a rack or a row facing the wrong way, tell the facilities or operations team rather than leaving it or fixing it yourself
the next time someone quotes a PUE, read it as total over IT energy and ask how much of the gap is cooling and what it does not tell you about the computing
the next time an AI capacity plan mentions liquid cooling, trace it in your head: chip, cold plate, rack loop, CDU, facility water, outside

persona.voice: the analyst as a peer explaining to colleagues: calm, exact, a little dry, the picture first and the name after
persona.delivery_notes: plain and level on the hook question; slow down and leave a beat on the open-slot leak and on the two loops; quick and light on the recap lines; warm, unhurried close

gagne.attention: hook: where does all that heat go, and what stops it coming back
gagne.objective: promise: follow the heat from one chip all the way outside
gagne.recall_prior: sec1 opens from the warm air behind a computer or a fridge
gagne.present: sections in dependency order: path, aisles and leaks, liquid, measure
gagne.guidance: signature move: ask where the heat goes next, follow it, then name the part
gagne.practice: pause_predict after sec2; faded beats in sec2 and sec3; payoff trace
gagne.feedback: the floor plan runs the predicted case and shows the back row breathing the front row's exhaust
gagne.assess: payoff: the viewer names each hand-off and leak before the narrator
gagne.transfer: transfer tasks: report an open slot, read a PUE, trace a liquid-cooling plan

merrill.problem_centered: the opening question, where does the heat go, runs through every section
merrill.activation: sec1 bridges from warm air behind everyday machines
merrill.demonstration: every hand-off is shown moving on screen before it is named
merrill.application: the viewer predicts the hottest row and spots the open slot
merrill.integration: transfer tasks put the path into the viewer's own floor walks and meetings

mayer.coherence: no vendor stories, no temperatures, no immersion detour; one rack, one floor plan, one chip
mayer.signalling: two slowdowns only, on the open-slot leak and the two loops
mayer.redundancy: screen shows the streams, parts and short labels; narration explains
mayer.contiguity: each part label appears on the part as it is named
mayer.segmenting: four sections, one hand-off idea each
mayer.pre_training: sec1 names intake, exhaust and cooling unit before the floor plan runs

arcs.attention: the heat question and visible warm and cool streams
arcs.relevance: AI capacity is the reason this room is changing; staff walk these floors and hear these numbers
arcs.confidence: one rack before a whole room, one chip before the whole loop
arcs.satisfaction: the viewer traces the full path unaided at the close
